name: Tetracycline
route_note: Oral capsules taken apart from food, dairy and antacids; eye ointment; topical preparations.
targets: 16S rRNA of the 30S ribosomal subunit (aminoacyl-tRNA A site)
originator: Pfizer (Lloyd Conover); also Lederle and Bristol

discovery.note: Obtained by catalytic hydrogenolysis of chlortetracycline, removing its chlorine; later also found to be produced naturally by Streptomyces.

tagline: Parent of the tetracycline class, now used mainly in eye ointment and H. pylori regimens
summary: Tetracycline is the namesake of a broad-spectrum antibiotic class derived from chlortetracycline in the early 1950s. Largely replaced by doxycycline for systemic use, it remains important in bismuth quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori and as eye ointment for trachoma and neonatal conjunctivitis prophylaxis.
mechanism: Tetracycline reversibly binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and prevents aminoacyl-tRNA from occupying the A site, inhibiting protein synthesis (bacteriostatic).

It chelates divalent and trivalent cations (calcium, magnesium, iron, aluminium), which impairs oral absorption and causes deposition in growing bones and teeth. Resistance is mediated by efflux pumps and ribosomal protection proteins, many on mobile elements.
uses: Helicobacter pylori eradication in bismuth quadruple therapy
Chlamydia, rickettsial infections, cholera and brucellosis (largely replaced by doxycycline)

history.title: Chlortetracycline
history.detail: Benjamin Duggar at Lederle reports chlortetracycline (Aureomycin).

history.title: Tetracycline synthesised
history.detail: Lloyd Conover at Pfizer produces tetracycline from chlortetracycline, a semi-synthetic antibiotic that is patented in 1955.

history.title: Antitrust
history.detail: A US Federal Trade Commission complaint follows over tetracycline pricing by several manufacturers.

history.title: WHO AWaRe classification
history.detail: WHO begins grouping antibiotics on its Essential Medicines List into Access, Watch and Reserve; tetracycline is a Access antibiotic.

pk.bioavailability: about 60–80% fasting; reduced by food, dairy, antacids and iron

serious: Permanent tooth discolouration and enamel hypoplasia in children and with fetal exposure
Hepatotoxicity in pregnancy at high doses

facts: Tetracyclines bind to newly formed bone and teeth and fluoresce under ultraviolet light, a property used in bone biopsy labelling.
